s: Today we learn five new body words.
They are small words, but you use them every day.
The five words are ear, tooth, finger, knee, and shoulder.
Let's start with word number one.
An ear is the part on the side of your head.
You have two ears, and I have two ears.
We hear music with our ears, and we hear our friends with our ears.
Do you hear the birds outside?
Your ears are small, but they do a big job.
With your ears you hear hello, you hear thank you, and you hear I love you.

A tooth is a hard white part in your mouth.
You bite food with your teeth.
I brush my teeth every morning, and I brush my teeth every night.
We eat apples with our teeth, and we eat bread with our teeth.
A tooth is strong, but candy can hurt your teeth.
My little brother lost a tooth last week.
He put the tooth under his pillow.
A finger is one of the five thin parts at the end of your hand.
I point with my finger, and I wave hello with my fingers.
My fingers help me every day.
You write with a finger, and you hold your cup with your fingers.
Your fingers are busy little helpers!
One finger, two fingers, three fingers, four fingers, five fingers.
Your fingers are great for counting.
Before word number four, here is a little more about the Muse English app.
Do you want to speak English with confidence?
The app gives you daily shadowing stories where you listen and repeat, sentence by sentence, in a clear studio voice.
There are grammar lessons with short examples and quizzes too.
Maya and I use the app every day.
Get the Muse English app and make English part of your morning!
A knee is the middle part of your leg.
When you sit down, your knees bend.
When you stand up, your knees help you.
They run and jump, and their knees are strong.
A shoulder is the part of your body between your neck and your arm.
I put my bag on my shoulder.
You can put your coat on your shoulders too.
A warm hug needs two shoulders!
And when you are tired, rest your head on a friend's shoulder.
Ear, you hear with your ears.
Tooth, you bite with your teeth.
Finger, you point with your finger.
Knee, it bends in your leg.
Shoulder, between your neck and your arm.
